html:
SMTO-SCH-0021 — Scheduling is disabled

GUID: 4e59d362-310e-4c9e-8f70-ecfc86563ad5
Slug: schedule-disabled
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • Scheduling is turned off for this SMTO server, so new schedules can't be made and existing ones can't be run or changed. Your saved schedules are kept, not deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules. If the top of the list says Scheduling is disabled, scheduling is off for the whole server. This confirms the problem is the server setting, not one schedule.
  2. Ask the person who installed or manages SMTO to turn scheduling on and restart SMTO. Scheduling is switched on in the server's setup, which only they can change.
  3. After the restart, open Schedules and check each schedule's Next run and target before relying on it. Schedules that were due while scheduling was off may now show a past or changed next time.

What success looks like

  • The Schedules page shows a count of your schedules instead of Scheduling is disabled, and New schedule can be selected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete your saved schedules; they are kept and will work again once scheduling is on.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Mission Control scheduling is disabled in this installation.

What this means

  • Schedule creation/inspection/API admission observes Agent event processing disabled in its effective configuration. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Schedule creation/inspection/API admission observes Agent event processing disabled in its effective configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owning events/scheduling setting and scope rather than creating another schedule ID.

How to fix it

  • Scheduling is gated by the AOR_AGENT_EVENTS_ENABLED server setting and the agent_events_enabled runtime control (RuntimeControlsService._events_enabled). If scheduling is intended, set AOR_AGENT_EVENTS_ENABLED=true, make sure the runtime control is not false, and restart the Server (the scheduler worker is installed at startup); then review each schedule's target and next trigger.
  • Enable scheduling through the existing scheduling configuration if intended, then review each schedule’s target and next trigger.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Authorized configuration enables the intended scheduling operation and its captured target is reviewed.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
